title: Turning, Cyclists & Pedestrians
whatItIs: A lorry can cause the greatest harm in a collision, so its driver carries the greatest responsibility. When you turn, give way to people crossing and never cut across cyclists.
keyFacts: Those who can cause the greatest harm bear the greatest responsibility. This applies most strongly to lorry drivers.
At a junction, give way to pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross the road you're turning into or out of.

keyFacts.text: You MUST give way to pedestrians on a zebra crossing, and to pedestrians and cyclists on a parallel crossing.

keyFacts: Don't turn if it would make a cyclist going straight ahead stop or swerve. Wait for a safe gap.
Overtaking cyclists: leave at least 1.5 metres at up to 30 mph, and more space at higher speeds.
Give cyclists and motorcyclists plenty of room, especially if you're driving a long vehicle.

items.title: Mirrors and signal early
items.text: Use your mirrors and give a left signal well before you turn.

items.title: Don't overtake, then turn
items.text: Never overtake just before you turn left. If you're behind a cyclist, stay behind.

items.title: Check down your left side
items.text: Watch for cyclists and others coming up on your left: they may be hidden from view.

items.title: Give way
items.text: To pedestrians crossing, and to anyone using a cycle lane, cycle track or bus lane.

a.label: Pedestrian at a junction
points: You should give way if they are crossing or waiting to cross
Once they have started to cross, they have priority

b.label: Pedestrian on a zebra crossing
points: You MUST give way once they are on it
You should also give way to those waiting to cross

onTheTest.question: You're turning left in your lorry. A cyclist is riding straight ahead in a cycle lane on your left. What should you do?
options: Give way and let the cyclist go ahead first
Turn quickly before the cyclist reaches the junction
Signal left and turn: the cyclist must stop
onTheTest.why: Give way to anyone using a cycle lane when you turn. Don't turn if it would make a cyclist going straight ahead stop or swerve.

onTheTest.question: You're overtaking a cyclist at 30 mph. What is the minimum space you should leave?
onTheTest.why: Leave at least 1.5 metres when overtaking cyclists at speeds of up to 30 mph, and give them more space at higher speeds.

traps: Signalling left doesn't give you priority over a cyclist going straight ahead.
Cyclists may ride in the centre of the lane on narrow roads, and they are not obliged to use cycle lanes.
Pedestrians who have started to cross the road you're turning into have priority.
In bad weather, high winds and at night, give cyclists and pedestrians even more space.
